summary:
1. Use vivid visual analogies in the very first sentence (e.g., '3 cars stacked on teeth') to boost retention (stayed_pct above 60%).
2. Frame titles and hooks around recognizable pop-culture tropes or direct user context ('your car', 'movies') rather than academic descriptions.
3. Write titles in Devanagari Hindi or conversational Hinglish with strong visual emojis rather than plain English news-style headlines.
4. Directly challenge a common belief in sentence one ('Movies show X, but reality is Y') to trigger immediate curiosity before the user swipes.
5. Keep dinosaur/prehistoric or extreme sensory comparisons as core topics while eliminating dry textbook language like 'hydroplaning' or 'microscopic structures'.
winning_hooks: Start with an immediate imagination prompt ('सोचो...') paired with extreme physical imagery ('3 cars on your teeth')
Debunk pop-culture myths immediately in sentence one ('Movies show T. rex chasing cars, but...')
avoid: English news-style title headlines ('Common Household Items That Contain...')
Jargon-heavy or academic Hindi openings ('वैज्ञानिकों को ऐसी सूक्ष्म आकृतियां क्यों मिली हैं...')
Weak passive openers without immediate personal framing or visual contrast
next_experiment: Test a direct visual-analogy hook vs. a myth-busting hook on the exact same topic, keeping both under 30 seconds and using identical Devanagari question titles.
